elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by Sparkling under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim." — the cap operates on "Each party", so both Vendor and Customer are capped, and no residual unlimited-Customer-liability language remains.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap is a single-limb "fees paid or payable ... in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim"; there is no "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor. To reach preferred, add the USD 1,000,000 alternative limb.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained p0105: "In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages ... including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use."

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Retained p0105: "The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14"; Section 14 is CONFIDENTIALITY, and the new cap sentence sits inside Section 15 so the carve-out reaches it.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list is limited to Sections 13 and 14 plus the newly added gross negligence and wilful misconduct; no data protection or security obligations are excluded from the cap.

"shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14"; Section 13 is INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY INDEMNITY, the Agreement's indemnity provision, so a failure to indemnify sits outside Section 15's limitation including the new cap.
Inserted: "The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall also not apply to a party's gross negligence or wilful misconduct."
Inserted: "... shall also not apply to a party's gross negligence or wilful misconduct."
Fraud does not appear in the carve-out sentence; only gross negligence and wilful misconduct were added alongside Sections 13 and 14.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Only the Section 13 "INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY INDEMNITY" heading is available; an IP indemnity ordinarily covers third-party infringement claims, not a party's own infringement of the other party's IP, and the body text is not rendered. An express carve-out for infringement of the other party's IP would be needed for preferred.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: No language states that Customer's obligation to pay fees is not "damages" for cap purposes; the new mutual cap on "total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement" is unqualified in that respect.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "Each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed ..." — expressly bilateral.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "the fees paid or payable by Sparkling under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — a 12-month fee basis; "fees" is used in its ordinary sense with no narrow defined term that would render the cap illusory.
Pre-existing retained sentence carves breaches of Section 13 (Intellectual Property Indemnity) out of "the limitation of liability in this Section 15", which now includes the inserted cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.

elements.evidence: Inserted second sentence expressly disapplies the Section 15 limitation to "a party's gross negligence".
Inserted second sentence expressly disapplies the Section 15 limitation to "wilful misconduct".

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the inserted mutual 12-month-fee cap plus the added gross negligence / wilful misconduct exclusions combine with the retained Sections 13 and 14 carve-out to cover all six fallback elements.

Preferred is not reached: no USD 1,000,000 alternative limb, no data protection/security carve-out, no fraud carve-out, no express carve-out for infringement of the other party's IP, and no statement that Customer's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.

Placement is sound — the cap is added inside Section 15 so the pre-existing sentence "The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14" governs the new cap; no dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence results.

Minimality holds: two sentences added, nothing deleted or paraphrased, no survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories or procedural boilerplate; the second sentence reuses the existing carve-out formula rather than duplicating it.

Intent preserved: the mutual consequential-damages exclusion, the direct-damages exclusive-remedy sentence and the risk-allocation recital survive unchanged, and the fee basis tracks the existing Fee Schedule.

Actionable note (rationale only, not a fallback defect): the unqualified mutual cap on "total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement" could be read to cap Customer's own obligation to pay fees; if raising to preferred, add "Customer's obligation to pay fees is not subject to this cap" together with the USD 1,000,000 floor and the data protection/security, fraud and other-party-IP carve-outs.
